memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Then you will remember to obey all my commands and will be consecrated to your God. I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of Egypt to be your God. I am the Lord your God.'" — Num 15:40-41 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter ends where all true obedience begins: with who God is. "I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of Egypt to be your God." Before God calls them to obey, He reminds them of what He has done for them. Obedience flows out of remembering His salvation.

This is the pattern of grace throughout Scripture. God does not say, "Obey Me, and then I will rescue you." He says, "I have rescued you; now, in response, walk in My ways." The command to be holy comes after the gift of redemption, never before it. Their obedience was to be a grateful response to a God who had already saved them, not a desperate attempt to earn His love.

Notice too the tender purpose in it all: "who brought you out of Egypt to be your God." He rescued them not merely from something but for something — for relationship with Himself. God's great desire was to be their God and to have them as His people. Every command was an invitation into that closeness.

This is the very heartbeat of the gospel. God, in Christ, has brought us out of a far worse slavery — out of sin and death — to be our God and to make us His own. We do not obey in order to be accepted; we are accepted in Christ, and so we obey out of love and gratitude. When obedience feels heavy, come back to these words: remember who your God is and what He has done. Let His grace be the fuel for your faithfulness. He brought you out to be your God — and He is.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you try to obey God to earn His love, or in response to His love?
2. How does remembering your redemption fuel your obedience?
3. What does it mean to you that God saved you "to be your God"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You rescued me not to earn Your love but because You already loved me, and You did it to be my God. Let my obedience flow from grateful remembrance of all You have done in Christ. You are the Lord my God. Amen.
